catalogue: The control catalogue — the controls the organisation implements — expressed as OSCAL catalog and profile content.
assessments: Assessment results, such as eval-gate runs, that record how each control was tested.
records: The evidence records the controls emit — verdicts and metrics — that back each assessment.
oscal: Layer 05 Assurance & Continuous Compliance: the OSCAL component-definition and assessment-results documents generated from that data, with traceability from a result back to the control it tested.
validator: The single gate: a validator that checks the OSCAL documents against the NIST JSON schema, so evidence is verifiable rather than hand-formatted.
auditor: The auditor, whose request for evidence becomes a filter over the store returned in minutes rather than a re-collection from scratch.
compliance: A continuous-compliance tooling category that ingests the OSCAL documents and tracks control status over time.
regulator: A regulator submission that reads the same documents, so evidence composes across tools and jurisdictions.
